Punon
PYOO-non
proper noun
Hebrew punon, of uncertain meaning, perhaps “darkness” or “perplexity,” a wilderness station of Israel in their journeys.

📖 Biblical Definition

Punon was one of the encampments of Israel in the wilderness, named in the record of their journeys that Moses wrote by the commandment of the LORD. As the people came up from the bondage of Egypt toward the borders of Edom, they pitched at Zalmonah, and then removed and pitched in Punon, and from Punon they journeyed and pitched in Oboth (Num 33:42-43). It lay in the desert region toward the land of Edom, one stage in the long wandering through which the LORD led and humbled and proved His people, to know what was in their heart. The dictionary records Punon, a bare name in a list of camps, that the reader may see how every stage of the pilgrimage was numbered and appointed by God. Not one resting place was forgotten, not one removal unordered; the cloud went before, and where it stayed, there Israel pitched. The lines of the wilderness journey were measured by the hand that determines the bounds of habitation, and Punon bears witness that the LORD knows the way that His people take, leading them by a right way to the city of their inheritance. The pilgrim saint may read this forgotten camp and be assured that his own stages, however bare, are numbered by his God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A wilderness encampment of Israel between Zalmonah and Oboth, toward the land of Edom.

expand to see more

PUNON, an encampment of Israel in the wilderness, in the desert region toward Edom.

It is named in the record of the journeys that Moses wrote by the commandment of the LORD.

Israel pitched there after Zalmonah and before they came to Oboth.

Its name is of uncertain meaning, perhaps “darkness” or “perplexity.”

It witnesses to the LORD’s numbering of every stage of His people’s pilgrimage.

📖 Key Scripture

Num 33:42 — "And they departed from Zalmonah, and pitched in Punon."

Psa 16:6 — "The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage."

Deu 32:8 — "When the Most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel."

Act 17:26 — "And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses to the LORD’s sovereign apportioning of every saint’s portion.

expand to see more

Punon is a place of the sacred geography, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it that the reader who meets the name in the list of Israel’s journeys may know it for a real camp in a real wilderness, where a real people pitched their tents at the bidding of a real God.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the providence of God over every stage of the pilgrimage. He who appointed Punon between Zalmonah and Oboth is the same who has determined the times before appointed and the bounds of every habitation. The saint upon his own bare and weary stages may remember this forgotten camp, and trust the God who numbers every removal and leads His people by a right way to the city of their rest.

"Like Punon in the wilderness, every bare stage of the saint’s pilgrimage is numbered by his God."

"The cloud that led Israel from camp to camp teaches us to follow the LORD step by step."

"A forgotten encampment reminds us that not one removal of the pilgrim is unordered by heaven."
